o: We must locate the single peak of a strictly-increasing-then-decreasing array, split there (peak counted in both halves), compare the two sums, and return 0, 1, or -1. In example 1 the peak is 3, giving sums 4 vs 6, so the answer is 1. In example 2 the peak is 5 giving 11 vs 7 -> 0; in example 3 both parts sum to 7 -> -1. Since n can be 1e5, an O(n) or O(n log n) scan is required; sums fit easily in 64-bit integers.
k: The peak is the unique index where nums[i] > nums[i+1] after the increasing run.
The peak belongs to both parts, so the two sums overlap by exactly one element.
Values up to 1e9 with n up to 1e5 mean sums need 64-bit accumulation.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear Scan for the Peak
a.i: Walk forward while the array keeps increasing; the walk stops exactly at the peak because the array is guaranteed bitonic. Then sum the prefix through the peak and the suffix from the peak and compare.
s: Advance pointer p while nums[p+1] > nums[p].
Sum nums[0..p] as the ascending part.
Sum nums[p..n-1] as the descending part.
Return 0, 1, or -1 depending on the comparison.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to find the peak plus two summation passes

a.n: Approach 2: Binary Search for the Peak
a.i: Because the array increases then decreases, comparing nums[mid] with nums[mid+1] tells which side of the peak mid lies on, so the peak can be found in O(log n) like a bitonic-search. Summation still takes O(n), so asymptotically it ties with the scan but does less work when the peak is late.
s: Binary search: if nums[mid] < nums[mid+1] the peak is right of mid, else at mid or left.
After the search, lo is the peak index.
Compute both sums around the peak and compare.
a.t: O(n) — O(log n) search dominates nothing since summation is O(n)

w: In an interview, the linear scan is the cleanest answer; mention binary search as an optimization of the peak-finding step only. Pitfalls: forgetting the peak counts in both sums, and using 32-bit sums (n * 1e9 overflows int). Follow-ups: what if the array were merely unimodal with plateaus, or you needed the split point minimizing |difference of sums|.
